questions.prompt: Complete: 'Our teacher ______ the register at the start of every lesson.'
questions.explanation: With 'our teacher' (he/she), we add -s to the verb: checks.

questions.prompt: A 'traffic light' helps to ______.
options: control cars and people on the road
questions.explanation: Traffic lights (red, yellow, green) control cars and people on the road.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A donkey is small than a camel.
A donkey is more small than a camel.
A donkey is smaller than a camel.
A donkey is smallest than a camel.
questions.explanation: Short adjective: small -> smaller, used with 'than' to compare two things.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Present perfect = has + past participle for 'he': He has washed.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'I think our team ______ the match on Saturday.'
questions.explanation: For a prediction we use 'will' + base verb: will win.

questions.prompt: A person who is 'confident' feels ______.
questions.explanation: Confident means feeling sure about yourself and your abilities.

questions.prompt: Which adverb means an action happens 100% of the time?
questions.explanation: 'Always' means the action happens every time, 100% of the time.

questions.prompt: Complete this diary line: 'Yesterday afternoon I ______ my uncle at the bus station.'
questions.explanation: A diary describes the past, so 'meet' becomes the irregular past 'met'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question.
options: Does Hana study at the library?
Do Hana studies at the library?
Does Hana studies at the library?
Does Hana studying at the library?
questions.explanation: After 'does', the main verb has no -s: Does Hana study at the library?

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Long ago, farmers ______ on the stars to know the seasons.'
questions.explanation: Verbs ending in consonant + y change y to i and add -ed: relied.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows a strong rule?
options: You can rest here for a while.
You should try the new dish.
Cyclists must wear a helmet on the highway.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a strong rule or obligation: must wear a helmet.

questions.prompt: Put the adverb correctly: 'sometimes'.
options: We help the neighbours sometimes help.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb: We sometimes help the neighbours.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'The road was blocked, ______ the bus took another route.'
questions.explanation: 'So' shows a result: the road was blocked, so the bus took another route.

questions.prompt: To behave in a 'polite' way means to be ______.
questions.explanation: Polite means behaving in a kind and respectful way to others.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that shows a plan already decided.
options: Maybe it will be cold tonight.
Our family is going to travel to Gondar next week.
I think he will agree with us.
Perhaps the shop will open early.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' shows a plan already made: is going to travel.

questions.prompt: If a bus station is 'congested', it is ______.
questions.explanation: Congested means very crowded and full of people or traffic.

questions.prompt: An animal that is 'endangered' is ______.
options: at risk of dying out completely
questions.explanation: Endangered means at risk of dying out completely; very few are left.

questions.prompt: A 'device' is ______.
options: a machine or tool made for a particular purpose
questions.explanation: A device is a machine or tool made for a particular purpose, such as a phone.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'She ______ just ______ her homework, so the books are still open.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect with 'she' = has + past participle: has just finished.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about a school sports day.
options: Aman is the faster runner in the class.
Aman is the most fast runner in the class.
Aman is the fastest runner in the class.
Aman is fastest runner in the class.
questions.explanation: For comparing many, use 'the' + adjective + -est: the fastest.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We have known each other since primary school.
We have known each other for primary school.
We have known each other from primary school.
We knew each other since primary school.
questions.explanation: Use 'since' with a starting point in time: since primary school.

questions.prompt: Change to the passive: 'Volunteers clean the park every weekend.'
options: The park clean every weekend by volunteers.
The park is cleaned every weekend by volunteers.
The park are cleaned every weekend by volunteers.
The park is clean every weekend by volunteers.
questions.explanation: Present passive = is/are + past participle; 'the park' is singular, so 'is cleaned'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I was very amazing by the experiment.
I were amazing by the experiment.
questions.explanation: The thing (the experiment) takes the -ing adjective: amazing.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that best shows the very last step of a recipe.
questions.explanation: 'Finally' introduces the last step or event in a sequence.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Students must to bring their books.
questions.explanation: A modal is followed by the base verb with no -s and no 'to': must bring.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'The strong wind ______ the old tree down during the night.'
questions.explanation: 'Blow' is irregular: its simple past is 'blew'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'The shops ______ closed because it was a public holiday.'
questions.explanation: Plural subject 'shops' (they) takes 'were': The shops were closed.

questions.prompt: What is the comparative of 'important'?
questions.explanation: 'Important' has three syllables, so the comparative uses 'more': more important.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Dawit kept playing ______ he was very tired.'
questions.explanation: 'Even though' shows a contrast: he kept playing even though he was tired.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: My brother carry water from the well.
My brother carrys water from the well.
My brother carries water from the well.
My brother carrying water from the well.
questions.explanation: Consonant + y in the third person changes y to i and adds -es: carries.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Did the workers built the bridge?
Did the workers build the bridge?
Do the workers built the bridge?
Did the workers building the bridge?
questions.explanation: After 'did', the main verb returns to its base form: Did the workers build?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: The Gelada baboon is more bigger than the wolf.
The Gelada baboon is bigger than the wolf.
The Gelada baboon is biggest than the wolf.
The Gelada baboon is the more big than the wolf.
questions.explanation: Never use 'more' with '-er'; use 'bigger than' to compare two animals.

questions.prompt: You suddenly decide to help a classmate carry her bag. Which sentence is best?
options: I am going to carry it for you.
I will carry it for you.
questions.explanation: For a decision made at the moment of speaking, we use 'will': I will carry it.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: Present perfect with 'we' = have + past participle 'seen': have never seen.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Marta lives in a small village. Every morning she walks two kilometres to school because there is no bus. She enjoys the walk when the weather is cool.' Why does Marta walk to school?
options: There is no bus in her village.
Her school is very far from the town.
She does not like riding bicycles.
questions.explanation: The passage says she walks 'because there is no bus'.

questions.prompt: Read: 'The new library opened last month. It has hundreds of books, and students may borrow two books at a time for one week.' How long can a student keep a borrowed book?
questions.explanation: The text states students may borrow books 'for one week'.
